sources.title: CVE-2026-82079
sources.snapshot: CVE Record 5.2, published 2026-09-10, updated 2026-09-11; CNA Nintendo.
sources.license: CVE record; cited.
sources.notes: Stack-based buffer overflow (CWE-121) in Nintendo Switch local wireless networking; affects versions before 23.0.0; CVSS 4.0 base score 7.0; solution is system update 23.0.0. CISA ADP lists exploitation as none at the record update.

sources.title: Nintendo security advisory: September 10, 2026

sources.license: Nintendo advisory; cited, not redistributed.

sources.title: jailbreaking the switch 2 (ns2jb)
sources.snapshot: Blog post dated 2026-10-18; retrieved 2026-10-26.
sources.license: Author's write-up; cited, not redistributed.
sources.notes: Primary technical write-up. States that ns2jb is a software-only, tethered Switch 2 jailbreak for 23.0.1 that runs native code as ordinary sysmodules and fs, without kernel access or CFW. Says the exploit was also tested on Switch 1 but has not been packaged.

sources.title: ns2jb repository
sources.snapshot: Repository created 2026-10-21; README retrieved 2026-10-26.
sources.license: No license was stated in the retrieved README; cited, not redistributed.
sources.notes: README states: Switch 2 only; requires SmileBASIC 4.4.9 and system software 23.0.1; the demo runs native functions inside FS and restores the original instructions; it does not install custom firmware or persistence.

sources.notes: Early Switch browser exploit toolkit. The README's documented launch paths target firmware 1.0.0 and the Fake News entry point, using a captive portal or DNS redirection. It is not a 23.0.1 entry point.

sources.title: Nintendo Switch Brew: Splay Applet
sources.snapshot: Documents the GameShare (splay) applet added with 20.0.0 and launched by qlaunch. States that it uses ldn and video streaming, that SetProtocol is used with value 3, that the host transfers the game NACP and JPEGs to the client during setup, and that ECC signature verification is used including for AdvertiseData from Scan. Lists the applet's IPC client services and notes that with 23.0.0+ the S1 applet gained news:c, stpl:sys, and FS permission bit47.
sources.license: Wiki text governed by Nintendo Switch Brew's terms; cited as documentation.
sources.notes: Primary technical description of the receive-side applet. It documents data flows, not vulnerabilities.

sources.title: Nintendo Switch Brew: 20.0.0
sources.snapshot: Change-log introduces GameShare: compatible software can be shared from a Nintendo Switch 2 to nearby systems, only over local wireless, and the Switch 2 must initiate. States the feature cannot be used between two Switch 1/OLED/Lite systems. Lists new title 0100000000001048 (splay), and notes that ns, migration, and splay use ldn SetProtocol with value 3.
sources.license: Wiki text governed by Nintendo Switch Brew's terms; cited as documentation.
sources.notes: Establishes when GameShare and the splay applet were introduced, and the host-model restriction.

sources.title: Nintendo Switch Brew: NPDM
sources.snapshot: Documents the NPDM format, including FsAccessControl and FsAccessFlag. Bit 47 is named StreamPlaySaveData.
sources.license: Wiki text governed by Nintendo Switch Brew's terms; cited as documentation.
sources.notes: Used to describe what a splay compromise would reach, not to claim that one exists.

sources.title: Nintendo Support: GameShare Overview and FAQ
sources.snapshot: States that a Nintendo Switch 2 system and compatible software are required to host a GameShare session. Only Switch 2 can share; it can share online to Switch 2 systems, or via local wireless to both Switch 2 and Switch systems.
sources.license: Nintendo support documentation; quoted as vendor documentation.
sources.notes: Establishes that the OLED can only be a receiver, and only over local wireless.

sources.title: Nintendo: Nintendo Switch 2 GameShare
sources.snapshot: Feature page describing GameShare as sharing supported games with nearby systems so that players who do not own the game can play.
sources.license: Nintendo product documentation; quoted as vendor documentation.
sources.notes: Consumer-facing description; used only for scope, not for technical detail.

sources.title: TwistedVoxel: Nintendo Removes SmileBASIC 4 From UK eShop Amid News Of Switch 2 Jailbreak
sources.snapshot: Published 2026-10-22. Reports that the UK eShop delisted SmileBASIC 4 after the ns2jb release, that the game remained listed in the US, Canada, and Mexico at the time of writing, and summarises the two-bug chain (SmileBASIC array integer overflow, filesystem path-normalization buffer overflow).
sources.license: News reporting; cited as secondary reporting.
sources.notes: Delisting status is time-sensitive and region-dependent. Treat store availability as volatile.

sources.title: TwistedVoxel: Nintendo Switch 2 Jailbreak Exploits Expand Beyond SmileBASIC 4, Developer Claims
sources.snapshot: Published 2026-10-23. Reports that Gezine said SmileBASIC 4 is not strictly necessary, naming Artemis Engine and an undisclosed physical game cartridge as alternate methods, and that Gezine advised against buying Artemis Engine for this purpose because save-based exploits could stop working if online services are blocked.
sources.license: News reporting; cited as secondary reporting.
sources.notes: Secondary reporting of social-media claims. No technical details, package, or reproduction is provided.

sources.title: Wccftech: Nintendo Doubles Down on Switch 2 Security, But Developer Gezine Cracks a Universal Exploit That Works Entirely Offline
sources.snapshot: Published 2026-07-20. Quotes Gezine saying he created a Switch 1/2 userland exploit that is not a WebKit or save exploit, that it works offline and across all firmware versions, and that it is not a full jailbreak by itself.
sources.license: News reporting; cited as secondary reporting.
sources.notes: The claim is attributed to the developer's social-media posts. No code, advisory, or technical write-up was found.

sources.title: Ars Technica: Switch 2 security takes a hit as hackers unlock homebrew access
sources.snapshot: Published 2026-10-22. Reports that ns2jb gains userland access, that it requires a macOS or Linux PC on the same network running a Node.js package, that the entry bug is a 32-bit integer overflow when removing array items in SmileBASIC, and that the exploit falls well short of kernel-level access.
sources.license: News reporting; cited as secondary reporting.
sources.notes: Independent coverage corroborating the userland-only capability boundary.

sources.title: TechSpot: Nintendo Switch 2 jailbreaking is here, with homebrew, modding, and reverse engineering
sources.snapshot: Published 2026-10-22. Reports that SmileBASIC 4 was delisted in the US and Europe soon after the Switch 2 jailbreak went public, so only people who already owned it can use that entry point.
sources.license: News reporting; cited as secondary reporting.
sources.notes: Corroborates the delisting and the resulting ownership constraint.

sources.title: Hacks Guide Wiki: Nintendo Switch models
sources.snapshot: States that only original Erista models made before July 2018 are currently hackable, that other patched Erista models may use the software method Caffeine on versions 4.0.0 to 4.1.0, and that Icosa (Mariko V2), Switch Lite (Hoag), and OLED (Aula) systems cannot be hacked via software at this time.
sources.license: Community wiki documentation; cited as a maintained guide.
sources.notes: Direct vendor-independent statement of the current software-hackability boundary for Mariko and OLED.

sources.title: liuervehc/caffeine: a warmboot exploit for system software 4.1.0 and below
sources.snapshot: README: 'an implementation of a warmboot exploit for Nintendo Switch running system software 4.1.0 and below (excluding 1.0.0)'.
sources.license: Open-source repository; cited as source code.
sources.notes: Establishes the warmboot-exploit category and its firmware range.

sources.title: Nintendo Switch Brew: Package1
sources.snapshot: Describes package1 as the first Switch bootloader plus the encrypted PK11 blob containing the second bootloader and TrustZone code. Section 0 contains the warmboot binary. States that on Mariko package1 is distributed in a custom, signed and encrypted format with an RSA-PSS signature.
sources.license: Wiki text governed by Nintendo Switch Brew's terms; cited as documentation.
sources.notes: Used to explain why a Mariko warmboot exploit is a distinct requirement from a bootROM bug.

sources.title: WikiTemp: List of Switch exploits
sources.snapshot: Historical list of Switch exploits: Jamais vu (1.0.0), PegaSwitch (1.0.0-3.0.0), Nereba (1.0.0-3.0.0), Déjà Vu / Caffeine (1.0.0-4.1.0, partially up to 7.0.1), and Fusée Gelée (non-iPatched consoles). Last edited 2019-08-07.
sources.license: GNU Free Documentation License 1.3 or later.
sources.notes: Useful for the historical sequence. It is stale and does not cover 23.0.1.

sources.title: Gezine/ArtemisLuaLoader: run arbitrary Lua script from save data
sources.snapshot: States that Artemis is a cross-platform visual-novel engine using Lua, that most Artemis games automatically load save9999.dat on boot, and that an edited save can chain-load inject.iet then inject.lua. Lists Windows, Android, iOS, Web, Nintendo Switch, and PlayStation as supported platforms, says testing was on Windows and PS4, and notes the repository is unmaintained and moved to shahrilnet/remote_lua_loader.
sources.license: Open-source repository; cited as source code.
sources.notes: A save-based script-loading mechanism, not a native-code chain. No Switch reproduction is documented.

sources.snapshot: Lists SmileBASIC 4 as Nintendo Switch download software.
sources.license: Nintendo store listing; quoted as vendor documentation.
sources.notes: Confirms the title is distributed as download software, so there is no physical cartridge route to obtain it.
